title: The Ember of Caerlum
premise: Kestrel Nystrom, junior ledger-keeper of the Guild of Caerlum — traders in impossible things — discovers that a century-old book of prophecies has recorded tonight's date and his own name beside an omen of war. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors who want the prophecy silenced and by the Ashen Court who want it fulfilled, Kestrel learns he is the illegitimate heir of the last Emberwright, the bloodline whose magic once burned the world. Choosing justice over law and truth over safety, he exposes the Inquisitor-General's forgery of history at the Conclave of Winter, then shatters the prophecy itself rather than let either side weaponize it. The guild survives diminished but honest, and Kestrel claims his inheritance on his own terms: as keeper of records, not maker of wars.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is a former archivist from the northern coast of England who writes fantasy steeped in ledgers, weather, and quiet rebellions. The Ember of Caerlum is her second novel and the first set in her long-planned world of the Ninefold Trade.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night audit in the guildhall of Caerlum establishes the dying guild, its impossible inventory, and Kestrel's careful, invisible life. He finds one entry that cannot exist: tonight's date, written a century ago. Beat: unease beneath routine.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. He compares the prophetic ledger to the guild's oldest codex and finds his own name in a dead woman's handwriting. Master Odell warns him to burn it; Kestrel cannot. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Already Here
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A stranger arrives holding the guild's token — issued only to the dead. He claims to be sent by the Ashen Court and asks for 'the Ember.' Kestrel lies for the first time in his life. Beat: first moral compromise.

chapters.title: What the Inquisitors Burn
chapters.summary: Wren (guild courier) POV. Crown Inquisitors raid a sister-guildhouse; Wren escapes with a scorched fragment naming the Emberwright line. She reaches Caerlum half-frozen. Beat: the outside world intrudes violently.

chapters.title: Blood in the Margins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Testing the fragment against guild blood-records, Kestrel confirms the impossible: the Emberwrights were not exterminated, they were absorbed — into guild families like his own. Beat: identity shaken.

chapters.title: Odell's Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel/Odell POV. The dying guildmaster admits he hid Kestrel's parentage for twenty years to keep him small and safe. Trust fractures. Beat: betrayal wrapped in love.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Snow falls out of season across the Ninefold Trade; roads close; superstition spreads. The prophecy's first sign is coming true without anyone casting it. Beat: dread made environmental.

chapters.title: A Fair Price for a Soul
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. To buy passage through closed roads, Kestrel trades a guild secret to a smuggler queen — breaking his first oath. He tells himself it's arithmetic. Beat: guilt rationalized.

chapters.title: The Ashen Court
chapters.summary: Sable Vane (Ashen envoy) POV. Inside the Court's hidden hall, Sable argues the prophecy must be fulfilled deliberately to end winter; her superiors prefer it fulfilled violently. Beat: antagonist given a sympathetic logic.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cross-referencing a century of entries, Kestrel proves the Inquisitor-General forged the historical record that condemned the Emberwrights. Truth becomes a weapon no one wants sheathed. Beat: resolve kindling.

chapters.title: The Road to Greyharrow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Kestrel flee toward the neutral Conclave city; an ambush by Inquisitors costs them their evidence copy. Wren saves Kestrel's life; something unspoken passes between them. Beat: bond forged under pressure.

chapters.title: What I Am
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cornered in a waystation, Kestrel's dormant Emberwright fire answers an attack — burning a man alive. He stares at his hands and does not recognize their owner. Beat: horror at the self.

chapters.title: The Kindness of Strangers
chapters.summary: Smuggler queen Maren's POV. Maren shelters them, having guessed what Kestrel is all along; she offers him an army of the lawless if he'll lead it. Justice outside the law tempts him. Beat: temptation of power.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable intercepts Kestrel privately: join the Court, control the fire, spare the guild. Her sincerity unsettles him more than threats would. Beat: the enemy becomes human.

chapters.title: Odell's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. News arrives that Odell died under Inquisitor interrogation without giving up Kestrel's name. Grief hardens into purpose; Kestrel takes the master's seal. Beat: mourning transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Conclave Assembles
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Delegates of guilds, Crown, and Court gather at Greyharrow while the unnatural winter deepens. Everyone carries a different version of history. Beat: tension of converging agendas.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Before the Conclave, Kestrel reads the forged record aloud and names the Inquisitor-General's fraud, using guild accounting methods as proof. The hall splits; blades come out. Beat: climax of truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Fire Answers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Inquisitor-General triggers the prophecy by force; Kestrel must embrace the Ember fully or watch Greyharrow burn. He chooses a third path: he burns the prophecy itself, severing its claim on the future. Beat: climax of sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Burning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The winter breaks unevenly; the Court splinters, the Crown retreats, and the guilds count their dead. Wren finds Kestrel alive but changed, his fire spent down to embers. Beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Offered restoration of the Emberwright name and lands, Kestrel declines both, accepting instead the guildmastership of a poor, honest Caerlum. Beat: identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Spring audits: debts forgiven, impossible things catalogued honestly, Wren installed as his partner in trade and in life. He writes the first page of a new ledger. Beat: quiet hope.

chapters.title: The Ember Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, years later. Teaching an apprentice, Kestrel keeps one secret: a faint warmth in his palms that never quite dies — held, not hidden. Some inheritances are carried, not spent. Beat: peace with ambiguity.
